territorial_scope.description: Binding and directly applicable in all EU Member States; applies to data centre operators with installed IT power demand of at least 500 kW.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

summary.short: The Regulation requires operators of data centres with at least 500 kW installed IT power demand to report defined information and sustainability indicators (energy, water, waste heat, renewables) to a European database, with first reports due 15 September 2024 and annual reporting thereafter.
summary.long: The Regulation defines the information and key performance indicators (KPIs) that operators of data centres with an installed information technology power demand of at least 500 kW must communicate to a European database, plus common measurement and calculation methods (Art. 1). Reports are due by 15 September 2024, then by 15 May 2025 and yearly, covering the preceding calendar year; they go through a national scheme where one exists, otherwise directly to the database (Art. 3(1)). In the first reporting periods, operators may omit listed KPIs for technical reasons with an explanation, and colocation operators may estimate coverage (Art. 3(2)-(3)). Annex I covers identification and redundancy; Annex II covers energy, water, waste heat, refrigerant, renewable energy, ICT capacity and traffic KPIs and requires measurement records kept for at least 10 years. Annex III defines PUE, WUE, ERF and REF. Aggregated data is published by Member State and Union level, by size category (Art. 5(2), Annex IV); individual data is kept confidential by the Commission and Member States (Art. 5(5)). It enters into force on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal (Art. 6).

notes: No amendment, repeal or replacement relations are stated in this text. Standards (CEN/CENELEC EN 50600 series) and Eurostat and Copernicus sources are cited for measurement methods and are not coded as relations. Internal inconsistencies: (1) Annex III(b) says WIN is 'as defined in Annex III' and EIT 'expressed in MWh', while WIN is defined in Annex II point 1(h) and EIT is measured in kWh in Annex II point 1(e). (2) The symbol TIN is used for intake air temperature in Annex II point 1(l) and for incoming data traffic in Annex II point 3(c). (3) Article 2(15) defines 'rated information technology load', while Annex II point 1(a) refers to 'rated information technology power demand'. (4) Article 1 covers data centres of at least 500 kW, but Annex IV lists a 'very small data centre' band of 100-500 kW. (5) The guarantees-of-origin definition in Annex II point 1(p) refers to the data centre measuring ERES-PPA.
